court: Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

issues.label: Jurisdiction over petition for review
issues.why: The court must confirm it has statutory jurisdiction to review the BIA's denial of the motion to reopen.

issues.label: Standard of review for motion to reopen
issues.why: Denials of motions to reopen are reviewed for abuse of discretion, framing the entire analysis.

issues.label: Legality of 'quantitative evidence' requirement
issues.why: The BIA invented a rule that CAT requires quantitative rather than anecdotal evidence, which may lack legal basis.

issues.label: Whether expert/anecdotal evidence properly discounted
issues.why: The BIA dismissed disturbing expert prison-conditions descriptions solely for being anecdotal, raising an evidentiary-weight error.

issues.label: Definition of 'new or previously unavailable' evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether continuation of pre-hearing abuse can constitute new evidence supporting reopening.

issues.label: Treatment of ongoing conditions as new
issues.why: Worsening or continuing conditions post-hearing may qualify as new material evidence despite predating the individual hearing.

issues.label: Materiality and prima facie case for reopening
issues.why: Reopening requires new evidence establishing a prima facie likelihood of eligibility for CAT relief.

issues.label: CAT 'more likely than not' torture standard
issues.why: The court must assess whether the BIA correctly applied the probability-of-torture standard on reopening.

issues.label: Aggregation of risk evidence
issues.why: CAT requires considering all evidence in the aggregate, not piecemeal dismissal of individual pieces.

issues.label: Consideration of country conditions evidence
issues.why: The prior remand faulted the IJ for ignoring country conditions, and improper exclusion may recur.

issues.label: Reasoned explanation for weight assignments
issues.why: The prior remand required adequate explanation for discounting expert reports, an obligation possibly violated again.

issues.label: Likelihood of detention finding
issues.why: The BIA found reasonable likelihood of detention, which bears on whether the torture analysis was internally consistent.

issues.label: State of Exception's legal significance
issues.why: The emergency crackdown context is central to assessing torture risk to detained deportees.

issues.label: Whether error was harmless
issues.why: The court must determine if any BIA errors affected the outcome or were harmless.

issues.label: Remand versus decision on record
issues.why: If the BIA erred, the court must decide the appropriate remedy or remand scope.

issues.label: Effect of equitable tolling grant
issues.why: The government's non-challenge to timeliness via tolling shapes what remains at issue.

issues.label: Relationship to Petition No. 24-7433
issues.why: The pending related petition for CAT/asylum denials may affect consolidation, mootness, or overlap.

issues.label: Deference to agency factual findings
issues.why: The court must apply substantial-evidence deference while distinguishing legal errors reviewed de novo.

issues.label: Chenery/agency-reasoning limitation
issues.why: Review is confined to the grounds the BIA actually articulated, not post-hoc rationalizations.

issues.label: Government-suffered vs. private torture; acquiescence
issues.why: CAT eligibility requires torture by or with consent/acquiescence of government officials.
